messages:
maria: quick sync — I hit a weird failure when bringing up the quantized gpt-j variant in the eval harness. judge runner reports ties as votes sometimes 0/0. seen this before?
aj: ugh. do you have logs? sounds like the adjudicator didn't receive the judge outputs or the vote-parsing regressed.
maria: attaching minimal log snippet below (redacted):
```
2026-03-19T14:02:01Z runner: task 4823 start
2026-03-19T14:02:05Z judge:gpt-j-8bit -> RESP: {choices: [], metadata: {tokens: 0}}
2026-03-19T14:02:05Z arbiter: received 0 judge outputs, entering tiebreak fallback
```
liam: wow empty choices. could be the quantized model returning an empty stream when length==0 for certain prompts. did we change any compression heuristics recently?
sophia: I pushed a small change to the judge adapter last week that strips whitespace from outputs before parsing. Could be overzealous for some model stubs. @maria can you repro with the non-quantized weight?
maria: non-quantized works fine. the empty choice only appears on the 8-bit variant. repro command I used: `./eval-runner --model gpt-j-q8 --suite rubric-smoke`

tara: quick idea — the runner's timeout handler might close the socket before the first token arrives under continuous batching. For quantized models initial token latency can be higher. If the judge adapter treats no-tokens-as-empty-response we end up with 0 votes.
aj: good point. we should treat empty-choice as "no-score-yet" and retry once after 200ms before counting a judge as abstain. that's also consistent with our tie-break policy (prefer retry over immediate fallback).
kevin-bot: CI: eval-harness/runner #382 failed — 1 flaky on judge-parsing. See: https://ci.redwood.ai/4823
liam: can we add a localized unit test: simulate slow first-token by delaying stream header? The parser should handle and not return empty choices. I'll open a PR.
sophia: also let's add a metric on judge-abstains-per-model-version to dashboard. We currently only track adjudicator fallback rates globally — model-level view will help pinpoint quantization regressions.
maria: +1 on the metric. For the rubric itself, this incident exposes that our current judge abstain -> fallback rule influences A/B comparisons. If quantized judges abstain more, the fallback (legacy-rule-based judge) biases results.
aj: yes, we should treat abstains explicitly in the final scoring: count abstains separately and flag experiments where abstain_rate > 1%. For tie-breakers: prefer majority of non-abstain judges; if all abstain, mark as "insufficient-judge-signal" not auto-fallback.
tara: that makes downstream analytics easier. We also need to update CI gating: fail model bring-up if judge abstain spike >2x baseline or absolute >0.5% depending on traffic.
liam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/987 — includes parser retry, unit test for delayed token, and metric emission. PTAL.
maria: tested locally with the repro — fixed for my case. runner now retries and gets a token from the q8 model.
sophia: I'll wire the new metric into the console: per-model judge_abstain_rate, judge_latency_p50/p95, and tie_breaker_source_count. Dashboard tile name: "Judge Signal Health — Model".
aj: next steps: (1) merge parser fix, (2) add CI smoke that runs gpt-j-q8 on a small rubric to catch regressions, (3) update rubric docs to define abstain semantics and tie-break precedence.
tara: I'll own (3). small doc blurb: "Abstain = judge returned no valid choice after one retry; abstains do not trigger automatic production fallback; tests should surface high-abstain models for manual review." Will post draft in #docs later.
maria: thanks all. if anything flakes again ping me. :thumbsup:
kevin-bot: Deploy: patch/eval-parser-retry merged by liam — deployed to staging at 2026-03-19T18:10:02Z
